name: Particle Background
css_code_snippet: .particle-bg { position: absolute; inset: 0; overflow: hidden; } .particle { position: absolute; width: 2px; height: 2px; background: var(--accent-1); border-radius: 50%; animation: drift var(--duration, 8s) linear infinite; opacity: 0; } @keyframes drift { 0% { transform: translateY(100vh) translateX(0); opacity: 0; } 10% { opacity: 0.8; } 90% { opacity: 0.4; } 100% { transform: translateY(-20px) translateX(var(--drift, 40px)); opacity: 0; } }
description: Animated floating particle field using absolutely positioned DOM elements driven by JS. Each particle gets randomized size (1-4px), duration (5-12s), and horizontal drift. Creates depth and ambient motion. Typically 60-120 particles for performance. Uses CSS custom properties for accent color.

name: Grid Overlay
css_code_snippet: .grid-overlay { position: absolute; inset: 0; background-image: linear-gradient(var(--grid-color, rgba(255,255,255,0.05)) 1px, transparent 1px), linear-gradient(90deg, var(--grid-color, rgba(255,255,255,0.05)) 1px, transparent 1px); background-size: 60px 60px; pointer-events: none; }
description: Pure CSS repeating grid lines using background-image gradients. Extremely lightweight. Works on both dark and light backgrounds by adjusting --grid-color opacity. Can be combined with perspective transform for a 3D vanishing-point effect. Grid size configurable via background-size.

name: Gradient Mesh
css_code_snippet: .gradient-mesh { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: radial-gradient(ellipse 80% 60% at 20% 30%, var(--accent-1, #4361ee) 0%, transparent 60%), radial-gradient(ellipse 60% 80% at 80% 70%, var(--accent-2, #7209b7) 0%, transparent 55%), radial-gradient(ellipse 100% 100% at 50% 50%, var(--bg-secondary, #131b3a) 0%, transparent 100%); animation: meshShift 12s ease-in-out infinite alternate; } @keyframes meshShift { 0% { filter: hue-rotate(0deg); } 100% { filter: hue-rotate(30deg); } }
description: Multi-layered radial gradient background creating an organic mesh effect. Three overlapping elliptical gradients blend at their edges. Slow hue-rotate animation adds life without distracting motion. No JS required. Pairs well with dark backgrounds where the gradients have room to glow.

name: Aurora Flow
css_code_snippet: .aurora-flow { position: absolute; inset: 0; overflow: hidden; } .aurora-flow::before, .aurora-flow::after { content: ''; position: absolute; width: 200%; height: 200%; top: -50%; left: -50%; background: conic-gradient(from var(--angle, 0deg) at 50% 50%, transparent 0deg, var(--accent-1, #00d4ff) 60deg, transparent 120deg, var(--accent-2, #ff2d78) 180deg, transparent 240deg); animation: auroraSpin 20s linear infinite; opacity: 0.15; filter: blur(40px); } .aurora-flow::after { animation-duration: 14s; animation-direction: reverse; opacity: 0.1; } @keyframes auroraSpin { to { --angle: 360deg; } }
description: Rotating conic gradient layers that simulate the northern lights effect. Two pseudo-elements rotate at different speeds and directions, creating an organic interference pattern. The heavy blur filter smooths the transitions into soft waves. Requires @property for --angle animation in modern browsers.

name: Noise Texture
css_code_snippet: .noise-texture { position: absolute; inset: 0; opacity: 0.04; background-image: url("data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg viewBox='0 0 256 256' xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%3E%3Cfilter id='noise'%3E%3CfeTurbulence type='fractalNoise' baseFrequency='0.9' numOctaves='4' stitchTiles='stitch'/%3E%3C/filter%3E%3Crect width='100%25' height='100%25' filter='url(%23noise)'/%3E%3C/svg%3E"); background-repeat: repeat; background-size: 256px 256px; mix-blend-mode: overlay; pointer-events: none; }
description: Inline SVG-based fractal noise texture applied as a repeating background with overlay blend mode. Adds organic grain and tactile quality to otherwise flat digital backgrounds. Nearly invisible at 4% opacity but noticeably adds depth. Increase opacity for editorial or analog aesthetics.

name: Dot Grid
css_code_snippet: .dot-grid { position: absolute; inset: 0; background-image: radial-gradient(circle, var(--dot-color, rgba(255,255,255,0.15)) 1px, transparent 1px); background-size: 28px 28px; pointer-events: none; }
description: Radial-gradient dot matrix pattern. Lighter and more refined than a line grid. Works on both light (dark dots) and dark (light dots) backgrounds. The 28px grid spacing is optimal for legibility — the dots register visually but don't compete with content. Zero JS, minimal CPU.

name: Wave SVG
css_code_snippet: .wave-svg { position: absolute; bottom: 0; left: 0; width: 100%; overflow: hidden; line-height: 0; } .wave-svg svg { display: block; width: calc(100% + 2px); height: 80px; } .wave-svg .wave-path { fill: var(--wave-color, rgba(255,255,255,0.05)); animation: waveMove 8s ease-in-out infinite; transform-origin: center bottom; } @keyframes waveMove { 0%, 100% { d: path('M0,40 C240,80 480,0 720,40 C960,80 1200,0 1440,40 L1440,80 L0,80 Z'); } 50% { d: path('M0,20 C240,60 480,20 720,60 C960,20 1200,60 1440,20 L1440,80 L0,80 Z'); } }
description: Animated SVG sine wave anchored to the bottom of a slide. Uses CSS path animation to morph between two wave shapes. Creates a gentle, organic motion that adds life without distraction. Best used as a subtle separator or section transition element in nature-adjacent and health aesthetics.

name: Neon Glow
css_code_snippet: .neon-glow { color: var(--neon-color, #00d4ff); text-shadow: 0 0 7px var(--neon-color, #00d4ff), 0 0 10px var(--neon-color, #00d4ff), 0 0 21px var(--neon-color, #00d4ff), 0 0 42px var(--neon-color-mid, #0080ff), 0 0 82px var(--neon-color-mid, #0080ff), 0 0 92px var(--neon-color-mid, #0080ff); animation: neonFlicker 3s infinite alternate; } @keyframes neonFlicker { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 92% { opacity: 1; } 93% { opacity: 0.8; } 96% { opacity: 1; } 97% { opacity: 0.6; } 99% { opacity: 1; } }
description: Multi-layer text-shadow stack that simulates a glowing neon tube. Layers progress from tight core glow to wide halo bloom. A subtle flicker animation at 3s intervals adds authenticity without being distracting. Color controlled via CSS custom properties for easy theming per slide.

name: Gradient Text
css_code_snippet: .gradient-text { background: linear-gradient(135deg, var(--grad-start, #4361ee) 0%, var(--grad-mid, #7209b7) 50%, var(--grad-end, #00d4ff) 100%); -webkit-background-clip: text; -webkit-text-fill-color: transparent; background-clip: text; background-size: 200% 200%; animation: gradientShift 4s ease infinite; } @keyframes gradientShift { 0% { background-position: 0% 50%; } 50% { background-position: 100% 50%; } 100% { background-position: 0% 50%; } }
description: CSS gradient clipped to text using background-clip. Animates the gradient position to create a flowing color shift effect on headlines. Works only on heading elements with solid or transparent backgrounds behind them. Three-stop gradient with configurable start/mid/end colors via custom properties.

name: Typewriter
css_code_snippet: .typewriter-text { overflow: hidden; border-right: 2px solid var(--cursor-color, #00d4ff); white-space: nowrap; animation: typeReveal var(--duration, 2s) steps(var(--chars, 30)) forwards, cursorBlink 0.75s step-end infinite; width: 0; } @keyframes typeReveal { to { width: 100%; } } @keyframes cursorBlink { 0%, 100% { border-color: var(--cursor-color, #00d4ff); } 50% { border-color: transparent; } }
description: CSS-only typewriter using width animation with steps() timing function to snap through character positions. A blinking border-right acts as the cursor. The --chars custom property must match the character count of the text for accurate stepping. Best for single-line code strings or key phrases.

name: Scramble Reveal
css_code_snippet: .scramble-text { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
description: JS-driven text scramble effect where each character cycles through random characters before resolving to its final value. Implementation: on trigger, iterate each character index with a setInterval; each tick randomizes the char from a charset (a-z0-9!@#$%); after n ticks per position, lock to final char. Creates a decoding/hacking aesthetic.

name: Split Color Text
css_code_snippet: .split-color-wrap { position: relative; display: inline-block; } .split-color-wrap .text-top { position: absolute; top: 0; left: 0; clip-path: inset(0 0 50% 0); color: var(--color-top, #ff2d78); } .split-color-wrap .text-bot { color: var(--color-bottom, #00d4ff); }
description: Dual-color horizontal split on a headline by layering two copies of the text and using clip-path to reveal only the top half of one and full view of the other. Creates a graphic two-tone effect popular in brutalist and retro design. No JS required; purely positional clipping.

name: Glass Card
css_code_snippet: .glass-card { background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.06); border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12); border-radius: 16px; backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(180%); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(12px) saturate(180%); box-shadow: 0 8px 32px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.1); transition: transform 0.2s ease, box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .glass-card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.15); }
description: Glassmorphism card using backdrop-filter blur and semi-transparent background. The inset top border creates a glass edge highlight. backdrop-filter requires a non-opaque background to be visible beneath. Hover state adds a subtle lift. Best on dark, gradient-rich backgrounds where the blur effect has texture to work with.

name: Neumorphic Card
css_code_snippet: .neumorphic-card { background: var(--bg-primary, #e8edf2); border-radius: 20px; box-shadow: 6px 6px 12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.15), -6px -6px 12px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7); padding: 1.5rem; transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease; } .neumorphic-card.pressed { box-shadow: inset 4px 4px 8px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.15), inset -4px -4px 8px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7); }
description: Soft UI / neumorphic card using dual box shadows — dark shadow on bottom-right, light shadow on top-left — to create an extruded effect from the background. Requires the card background to exactly match the slide background. An inset variant simulates a pressed/active state.

name: Clay 3D Card
css_code_snippet: .clay-card { border-radius: 24px; background: var(--clay-color, #ffffff); box-shadow: 0 20px 60px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.15), 0 6px 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1), inset 0 -4px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1), inset 0 2px 4px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.6); transform: translateZ(0); transition: transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1), box-shadow 0.3s ease; } .clay-card:hover { transform: translateY(-8px) scale(1.02); box-shadow: 0 30px 80px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2), 0 10px 30px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.12), inset 0 -4px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.08), inset 0 2px 4px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7); }
description: 3D clay-style card using layered box shadows including a bottom inset shadow to simulate thickness, and a top inset highlight for the clay sheen. The hover state uses a spring-like cubic-bezier for a playful, physical bounce. Popular in modern product and consumer app presentations.

name: Brutalist Shadow
css_code_snippet: .brutalist-card { border: 3px solid #0a0a0a; background: #ffffff; box-shadow: 6px 6px 0 #0a0a0a; transition: transform 0.1s ease, box-shadow 0.1s ease; cursor: pointer; } .brutalist-card:hover { transform: translate(3px, 3px); box-shadow: 3px 3px 0 #0a0a0a; } .brutalist-card:active { transform: translate(6px, 6px); box-shadow: 0 0 0 #0a0a0a; }
description: Hard offset box shadow with no blur radius — the defining brutalist card treatment. Solid black border matches the shadow color for a stacked paper effect. On hover, the card slides toward its shadow, simulating a press. On active, it fully depresses. No border-radius for raw, graphic geometry.

name: Holographic Border
css_code_snippet: .holo-card { position: relative; border-radius: 16px; background: var(--bg-secondary); padding: 1px; } .holo-card::before { content: ''; position: absolute; inset: -1px; border-radius: 17px; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #00ffcc, #ff00aa, #4361ee, #00d4ff, #ff2d78, #00ffcc); background-size: 300% 300%; animation: holoShift 4s linear infinite; z-index: -1; filter: blur(1px); } @keyframes holoShift { 0% { background-position: 0% 50%; } 100% { background-position: 300% 50%; } }
description: Animated rainbow gradient border using a pseudo-element slightly larger than the card with a wide linear-gradient animating its background-position. The card content sits on top on a solid background color. The filter blur softens the border slightly for a glowing holo effect.

name: Fade Up
css_code_snippet: .fade-up { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(30px); transition: opacity 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), transform 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .fade-up.visible { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); }
description: The most universally applicable entrance animation. Element starts at 30px below and zero opacity, transitions to natural position with ease-out spring curve. Trigger by adding .visible class via IntersectionObserver or slide-enter event. Stagger multiple elements by adding transition-delay increments (0.1s per item).

name: Scale In
css_code_snippet: .scale-in { opacity: 0; transform: scale(0.85); transition: opacity 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1), transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1); } .scale-in.visible { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1); }
description: Scale from 85% to 100% with a spring overshoot curve (cubic-bezier with control points beyond 1.0). Creates a confident, energetic pop-in feel. Best for hero elements, icons, metric numbers, and CTA buttons. The spring curve makes it feel physical without requiring a JS animation library.

name: Slide Left
css_code_snippet: .slide-left { opacity: 0; transform: translateX(-40px); transition: opacity 0.5s ease-out, transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .slide-left.visible { opacity: 1; transform: translateX(0); }
description: Horizontal entrance from left. Useful for content panels in split layouts where the left column should appear first, then the right panel slides in from the opposite direction. Combine with slide-right on the opposing panel and a 0.15s delay for a satisfying bilateral reveal.

name: Blur In
css_code_snippet: .blur-in { opacity: 0; filter: blur(8px); transform: scale(1.05); transition: opacity 0.7s ease, filter 0.7s ease, transform 0.7s ease; } .blur-in.visible { opacity: 1; filter: blur(0px); transform: scale(1); }
description: Combines defocus blur with slight scale-down for a dreamy focus-pull entrance effect. Popular in architectural, editorial, and atmospheric presentations. The 1.05 starting scale combined with the blur creates the illusion of depth of field being pulled into focus. Slightly slower (0.7s) for cinematic pacing.

name: Glitch In
css_code_snippet: .glitch-in { animation: glitchReveal 0.6s steps(1) forwards; } @keyframes glitchReveal { 0% { opacity: 0; clip-path: inset(40% 0 40% 0); transform: translateX(-8px); } 20% { opacity: 1; clip-path: inset(10% 0 80% 0); transform: translateX(8px); } 40% { clip-path: inset(80% 0 5% 0); transform: translateX(-4px); } 60% { clip-path: inset(30% 0 30% 0); transform: translateX(4px); } 80% { clip-path: inset(0% 0 0% 0); transform: translateX(0); } 100% { clip-path: none; transform: translateX(0); opacity: 1; } }
description: Stepped clip-path animation that creates a horizontal scan-bar glitch effect on entrance. The steps() timing function snaps between states without interpolation for a digital artifact look. Clip-path slices reveal different horizontal bands in rapid succession. Self-contained CSS, no JS required.

name: Flip In
css_code_snippet: .flip-in { perspective: 800px; } .flip-in-inner { opacity: 0; transform: rotateX(-90deg); transform-origin: top center; transition: opacity 0.5s ease, transform 0.5s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1); } .flip-in-inner.visible { opacity: 1; transform: rotateX(0deg); }
description: 3D flip entrance using rotateX on a child element inside a perspective wrapper. The element appears to unfold from the top edge into its natural position. The spring cubic-bezier gives it a satisfying bounce at the end. Particularly effective for card reveals in grid layouts and flashcard-style educational slides.

name: Floating Shapes
css_code_snippet: .floating-shape { position: absolute; border-radius: 50%; opacity: 0.15; animation: float var(--float-dur, 6s) ease-in-out infinite alternate; } @keyframes float { 0% { transform: translateY(0) rotate(0deg) scale(1); } 100% { transform: translateY(var(--float-y, -30px)) rotate(var(--float-rot, 15deg)) scale(var(--float-scale, 1.1)); } }
description: Soft, slowly floating geometric shapes (circles, blobs, rounded rectangles) that drift in alternating directions using CSS alternate animations. Each shape gets randomized --float-dur (5-9s), --float-y (-20 to -50px), --float-rot (10-25deg), and --float-scale (1.05-1.15) via JS initialization. Creates ambient movement without distraction.

name: Pulsing Rings
css_code_snippet: .pulsing-ring { position: absolute; border-radius: 50%; border: 1px solid var(--ring-color, rgba(0, 212, 255, 0.4)); animation: ringPulse 3s ease-out infinite; } .pulsing-ring:nth-child(2) { animation-delay: 1s; } .pulsing-ring:nth-child(3) { animation-delay: 2s; } @keyframes ringPulse { 0% { transform: scale(0.5); opacity: 0.8; } 100% { transform: scale(2.5); opacity: 0; } }
description: Three concentric rings that expand and fade in sequence, creating a radar/sonar ping effect. Each ring is offset by 1s delay to create a continuous outward pulse. Best placed around a central icon or logo on hero slides. Color controlled via --ring-color custom property. Pure CSS, no JS.

name: Scanning Line
css_code_snippet: .scanning-line-wrap { position: absolute; inset: 0; overflow: hidden; pointer-events: none; } .scanning-line { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; height: 2px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, var(--scan-color, rgba(0, 212, 255, 0.6)), transparent); animation: scanDown 4s linear infinite; } @keyframes scanDown { 0% { top: -2px; } 100% { top: 100%; } }
description: A single horizontal line that sweeps top to bottom on a loop, simulating a radar scan or document scanner. The gradient fades to transparent at both ends. Paired well with dark backgrounds and terminal/tech aesthetics. Can be reversed (scanUp) or doubled for bidirectional effect. Pure CSS.

name: 3D Tilt
css_code_snippet: .tilt-card { transform-style: preserve-3d; transform: perspective(1000px); transition: transform 0.1s ease; will-change: transform; } .tilt-card .tilt-layer { transform: translateZ(20px); }
description: Mouse-tracking 3D card tilt effect. JS listens to mousemove on the card, calculates normalized cursor position (−1 to 1 on both axes), and sets CSS transform: perspective(1000px) rotateX(Ydeg) rotateY(Xdeg). Inner elements with translateZ create parallax depth layers. On mouseleave, spring back to 0,0 with a brief transition.

name: Magnetic Hover
css_code_snippet: .magnetic-btn { display: inline-block; transition: transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1); cursor: pointer; }
description: JS-driven magnetic attraction effect where the element gently follows the cursor when the mouse is within a defined radius (typically 80-100px). On mousemove, calculate distance from element center to cursor; if within radius, translate the element proportionally (max 15-25px). On mouseleave, spring back. Best for CTA buttons and key interactive elements.

name: Ripple Click
css_code_snippet: .ripple-container { position: relative; overflow: hidden; } .ripple { position: absolute; border-radius: 50%; width: 4px; height: 4px; background: var(--ripple-color, rgba(255,255,255,0.3)); transform: scale(0); animation: rippleExpand 0.6s linear; pointer-events: none; } @keyframes rippleExpand { to { transform: scale(var(--ripple-scale, 100)); opacity: 0; } }
description: Material Design-style click ripple. On click, JS creates a .ripple div positioned at the click coordinates within the container, sets --ripple-scale based on container size, then removes the element after animation completes. Creates satisfying tactile feedback for interactive presentation elements like buttons and cards.

name: Parallax Scroll
css_code_snippet: .parallax-layer { will-change: transform; transition: transform 0.1s linear; } .parallax-layer[data-speed='0.5'] { /* moves at 50% of scroll speed */ } .parallax-layer[data-speed='1.5'] { /* moves at 150% of scroll speed */ }
description: Layered depth effect where background elements move slower than foreground elements during scroll. JS maps scroll position to translateY values per layer using the data-speed multiplier. Speed < 1 creates the illusion of depth recession; speed > 1 creates a foreground zoom-past feel. Best used sparingly with 2-3 distinct depth layers.

name: Chart Reveal
css_code_snippet: .chart-bar { transform-origin: bottom; transform: scaleY(0); animation: barGrow 0.8s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) forwards; } .chart-line { stroke-dasharray: var(--line-length); stroke-dashoffset: var(--line-length); animation: lineTrace 1.2s ease-out forwards; } @keyframes barGrow { to { transform: scaleY(1); } } @keyframes lineTrace { to { stroke-dashoffset: 0; } }
description: Two-mode chart animation: bar charts use scaleY from transform-origin bottom for a growing bar effect; line charts use SVG stroke-dashoffset animation to trace the line path. The --line-length must be set to the SVG pathLength via JS on mount. Stagger bar animations by index * 0.08s for a sequential reveal.

name: Number Counter
css_code_snippet: .counter-number { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
description: JS-driven count-up animation for metric numbers. On trigger, read the target value from data-target attribute, then use requestAnimationFrame with an easeOutQuart curve to increment from 0 (or a lower starting value) to the target over ~1.5s. Handles integers, decimals, currency prefixes, and % suffixes. Tabular-nums ensures stable width during count.

name: Progress Bar
css_code_snippet: .progress-track { background: var(--track-color, rgba(255,255,255,0.1)); border-radius: 99px; overflow: hidden; } .progress-fill { height: 6px; border-radius: 99px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, var(--accent-1), var(--accent-2)); width: 0%; transition: width 1.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .progress-fill.animate { width: var(--target-width); }
description: Animated horizontal progress bar for showing completion percentages, skill levels, or agenda progress. The fill element transitions from 0% to the --target-width value when .animate is added. Gradient fill uses accent colors. Track has a subtle transparent background. Add a counter label that updates in sync for dual reinforcement.

name: Confetti
css_code_snippet: .confetti-piece { position: absolute; width: 10px; height: 10px; animation: confettiFall var(--fall-dur, 3s) linear var(--fall-delay, 0s) forwards; } @keyframes confettiFall { 0% { transform: translateY(-20px) rotate(0deg); opacity: 1; } 100% { transform: translateY(110vh) rotate(var(--spin, 720deg)); opacity: 0.2; } }
description: JS generates 80-150 confetti pieces with randomized colors (6 colors from the active palette), sizes (6-14px), shapes (square/circle/ribbon via border-radius), fall durations (2-4s), delays (0-2s), horizontal positions (0-100%), and spin amounts (360-1080deg). Triggered on a celebration moment like the final slide or key reveal.
